summaries.information_need: A researcher wants to understand the motivation behind the CARR model, a dynamic range-based volatility specification proposed to fill the gap between the well-established GARCH family of models and the long-recognized but historically poorly performing use of the price range as a volatility estimator.

A researcher wants the CARR model specification for the dynamic conditional mean of the price range, expressed as a multiplicative-error autoregressive structure analogous to GARCH and the autoregressive conditional duration model, together with its stationarity condition and its extension to include exogenous explanatory variables.

A researcher wants to know why quasi-maximum likelihood estimation of the CARR model is consistent under an assumed exponential density for the disturbance, and why this estimation is equivalent to fitting a particular GARCH specification, together with the correct way to obtain robust standard errors for the estimated coefficients.

A researcher wants the Weibull distribution CARR model as a more flexible alternative to the exponential specification for the range disturbance, together with the resulting relationship between CARR and the standard deviation GARCH model and the fairness concerns that arise when comparing the two models' forecasts given their different information sets.

An analyst wants summary statistics on range persistence for a weekly stock index series compared to absolute returns, measured through autocorrelation functions and Ljung-Box statistics, to establish that the raw range exhibits far stronger volatility clustering than absolute returns before any dynamic model is fitted.

An analyst wants ECARR model estimation results for a weekly stock index range series across several lag orders and exogenous-variable specifications, focused on whether the fitted model removes the strong persistence found in the raw range and whether a leverage effect from lagged returns is statistically significant.

An analyst wants WCARR model estimation results using a Weibull distribution for the range disturbance, compared against the exponential specification through goodness-of-fit tests, together with evidence on whether the choice between the two error distributions materially changes the resulting in-sample range forecasts.

summaries.field: applied financial econometrics / volatility forecast evaluation
summaries.information_need: An analyst wants the design of an out-of-sample forecast comparison between the CARR and GARCH models across multiple forecast horizons ranging from one week to fifty weeks, using rolling-sample parameter estimation, as a setup for evaluating which model produces more accurate volatility forecasts across several measured volatility benchmarks.

summaries.field: applied financial econometrics / volatility forecast evaluation
summaries.information_need: An analyst wants a forecast accuracy comparison between ECARR and GARCH volatility forecasts across four different measured-volatility benchmarks, evaluated using root-mean-squared-error and mean-absolute-error criteria at several forecast horizons, to see which model consistently produces smaller forecast errors.

summaries.field: applied financial econometrics / volatility forecast evaluation
summaries.information_need: An analyst wants Mincer-Zarnowitz regression results that assess the predictive power of ECARR versus GARCH volatility forecasts against four measured-volatility benchmarks, together with a forecast encompassing regression specification used to determine whether one model's forecast contains information not already present in the other's.

summaries.field: applied financial econometrics / volatility forecast evaluation
summaries.information_need: An analyst wants the encompassing regression results comparing ECARR and GARCH volatility forecasts jointly, to determine whether the GARCH forecast retains any explanatory power once the ECARR forecast is included, together with the overall conclusion on which model provides sharper out-of-sample volatility forecasts.

A researcher wants an overview of future research extensions for the CARR model, including robust measures of range less sensitive to outliers and an extension that incorporates opening and closing prices to jointly model a time-varying drift alongside the range-based volatility process.
